claim: For every finite ordinal \(n<\omega\), the ordinal-indexed fixed-point proof system \(\mu\mathrm{MALL}_{n,n}\) has an effective finite translation to ordinary MALL preserving provability, uniformly in \(n\); hence the combined finite-stage theoremhood problem is decidable. At the first infinite stage \(\alpha=\omega\), theoremhood is \(\Sigma^0_{\omega^{\omega^\omega}}\)-complete under Turing reductions.

integrity: The finite-stage proof is an explicit finite-approximation translation.
No claim of independent verification or certification is made.
limitations: No optimal time or space complexity is proved for the finite-stage decision procedure.
The transfinite complexity statement at the first infinite stage is cited from the primary paper, not independently reproved.
Independent audit has not been performed.

title: Finite ordinal stages of \(\mu\mathrm{MALL}_{n,n}\) collapse to MALL before the first infinite branching level
